description: Structured canonical radiation oncology dose fractionation schemes, definitive vs adjuvant target dose prescriptions, and radiobiological principles extracted from authoritative radiation oncology textbooks (Perez & Brady 2026 8th Ed, Gunderson & Tepper 5th Ed, 2026 Essentials of Clinical Radiation Oncology 2nd Ed, Kogel Basic Clinical Radiobiology 2019 5th Ed, Hall & Giaccia Radiobiology for the Radiologist 8th Ed).

linear_quadratic_model.description: Cell survival model describing radiation-induced clonogenic cell death. Alpha represents the linear single-track lethality (lethal unrepairable DNA double-strand breaks), Beta represents the quadratic two-track lethality (interaction between two independent sublethal lesions).
linear_quadratic_model.alpha_beta_ratio_definition: The dose (d = alpha / beta) in Gray at which the linear (alpha * d) and quadratic (beta * d^2) components contribute equally to cell kill.

biologically_effective_dose.formula: BED = Total_Dose * (1 + (dose_per_fraction / (alpha_beta))) = n * d * (1 + d / (alpha / beta))
biologically_effective_dose.units: Gy_alpha_beta (e.g. Gy10 for tumors/acute effects, Gy3 or Gy2 for late-reacting normal tissues)
biologically_effective_dose.incomplete_repair_extension: BED = n * d * [1 + (d / (alpha / beta)) * (1 + h_m)] where h_m is the Lea-Catcheside incomplete repair factor accounting for sub-complete recovery during multiple fractions per day (<6-8 hours interval) with mono- or bi-exponential half-times (T1/2 ~ 0.5-1.5 hours).

equivalent_dose_in_2gy_fractions.clinical_utility: Universal metric allowing comparison and summing of doses delivered across different fractionation regimens, hypofractionation, SBRT, and brachytherapy.

proliferation_and_time_factor.formula: BED_corrected = BED - (ln(2) / (alpha * T_pot)) * (T_overall - T_kickoff) = BED - D_prolif * (T_overall - T_k)

parameters.T_k: Kick-off onset time of accelerated tumor clonogen repopulation (~21 to 28 days in squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck and cervix).
parameters.D_prolif: Equivalent dose required to offset daily repopulation after kick-off, approximately 0.6 Gy/day (range 0.5-0.8 Gy/day) in head and neck SCC.
parameters.clinical_rule: Unplanned treatment interruptions or prolongation of overall treatment time result in an estimated 1.0% to 1.5% decrease in local tumor control per day of delay.

the_classical_and_modern_rs_of_radiobiol.mechanism: Sublethal damage repair (SLDR) in normal tissues versus tumors between fractions. Late-responding normal tissues have large repair capacity (low alpha/beta ~ 2-3 Gy), so smaller fraction sizes selectively spare late complications.

Cells arrest or survive in radioresistant phases (late S phase); with time between fractions, surviving cells redistribute into radiosensitive phases (G2/M), increasing efficacy of subsequent fractions.
Accelerated proliferation of tumor clonogens during protracted courses. Minimizing overall treatment time (OTT) prevents repopulation from compromising tumor control.
Hypoxic tumor cells (resistant due to lack of oxygen fixation, OER 2.5-3.0) reoxygenate between fractions as aerated cells die and metabolic demand falls, restoring radiosensitivity.
Inherent cellular and genetic susceptibility to ionizing radiation, quantified by the surviving fraction at 2 Gy (SF2).
Modern 6th R: Radiation induces immunogenic cell death (calreticulin exposure, HMGB1, ATP release) and cGAS-STING activation, priming CD8+ T-cell responses.

key_passages.text: The linear-quadratic (LQ) model describes the survival fraction S = exp(-alpha*d - beta*d^2). The ratio alpha/beta governs the sensitivity of a tissue to changes in dose per fraction. Low alpha/beta values (~2-3 Gy) characterize late-responding normal tissues, whereas high alpha/beta values (~10 Gy) characterize early responses and most tumors.

key_passages.chapter: Chapter 10: The linear-quadratic approach in clinical practice
key_passages.text: EQD2 is defined as the total dose delivered in 2 Gy fractions that produces the same biological effect as a schedule of D delivered in fractions of d: EQD2 = D * (d + alpha/beta) / (2 + alpha/beta). Biologically effective dose is BED = D * (1 + d / (alpha/beta)).

key_passages.chapter: Chapter 12: Time factors in normal tissue responses to irradiation
key_passages.text: Proliferation during radiotherapy becomes significant after a delay or kick-off time Tk of approximately 3 to 4 weeks in squamous cell carcinomas. Compensation for missed fractions requires hyperfractionation or dose escalation of approximately 0.6 Gy per day lost.

oxygen_effect.definition: Oxygen Enhancement Ratio (OER) = Dose in hypoxia / Dose in air for identical biological effect.
oxygen_effect.typical_values: OER is 2.5 to 3.0 for sparsely ionizing radiations (X-rays, gamma rays) at high doses, declining to ~2.0 at doses <2 Gy, and approaches 1.0 for high-LET radiations.
oxygen_effect.clinical_significance: Severe hypoxia (pO2 < 5-10 mmHg) renders tumor core cells 2.5 to 3-fold more radioresistant. Fractionation permits reoxygenation of previously hypoxic tumor cells.

dna_repair_pathways.non_homologous_end_joining: Dominant pathway in G0/G1 and early S phase. Direct re-ligation without template, rapid (T1/2 ~ 15-30 min), error-prone.
dna_repair_pathways.homologous_recombination: Dominant in late S and G2 phase. Uses undamaged sister chromatid as template, high fidelity, error-free.

cell_cycle_dependence.most_sensitive: M phase (mitosis) and late G2 phase.
cell_cycle_dependence.most_resistant: Late S phase (elevated intracellular radical scavengers, e.g. glutathione, and homologous recombination repair mechanisms).

linear_energy_transfer_and_rbe.let_definition: Rate of energy loss along the track of an ionizing particle (keV/micrometer).
linear_energy_transfer_and_rbe.rbe_peak: RBE reaches a maximum (~100 keV/micrometer) where average distance between ionizations matches diameter of DNA double helix (2 nm), producing clustered non-repairable complex lesions.

key_passages.chapter: Chapter 6: The Oxygen Effect and Reoxygenation
key_passages.text: For oxygen to act as a radiosensitizer, it must be present during radiation exposure or within microseconds thereafter. The oxygen fixation hypothesis posits that radiation produces free radicals in target DNA that are 'fixed' into permanent organic peroxides by molecular oxygen.

key_passages.chapter: Chapter 8: The Linear-Quadratic Model and Fractionation
key_passages.text: The shoulder of the survival curve is primarily reflected in the beta parameter. Sparing of late responding tissues by hyperfractionation exploits the shallow initial slope and steep curvature (low alpha/beta ratio) of late normal tissues.

entries.title: Perez, Brady, Halperin, and Wazer's Principles and Practice of Radiation Oncology

standard_fractionation.primary_gross_disease_ptv_high: 70 Gy in 35 fractions (2.0 Gy/fraction) over 7 weeks
standard_fractionation.concurrent_systemic: High-dose cisplatin 100 mg/m2 IV every 3 weeks (days 1, 22, 43) or weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m2 IV

altered_fractionation.hyperfractionation: 81.6 Gy in 68 fractions (1.2 Gy/fraction twice daily with >=6 hours gap) (RTOG 9003 / MARCH meta-analysis)
altered_fractionation.accelerated_concomitant_boost: 72 Gy in 42 fractions over 6 weeks (1.8 Gy/fx large field + 1.5 Gy/fx boost twice daily for last 12 treatment days)
altered_fractionation.early_glottic_t1n0: 66 Gy in 33 fractions (2.0 Gy/fx) or hypofractionated 63 Gy in 28 fractions (2.25 Gy/fx) or 58.5-60 Gy in 25 fractions (2.34-2.4 Gy/fx)
altered_fractionation.glottic_t2n0: 70 Gy in 35 fractions (2.0 Gy/fx) or 65.25 Gy in 29 fractions (2.25 Gy/fx)

standard_intermediate_risk.dose: 56 to 60 Gy in 28 to 30 fractions (1.8-2.0 Gy/fraction)
standard_intermediate_risk.indications: Perineural invasion, lymphovascular invasion, close margins (<=2 mm), multiple involved lymph nodes without extracapsular extension (ECE)

high_risk.dose: 66 Gy in 33 fractions (2.0 Gy/fraction) to high-risk bed / ECE sites; 54-56 Gy to elective nodal basins
high_risk.indications: Positive microscopic surgical margin (R1) or extracapsular nodal extension (ECE/ENE)
high_risk.concurrent_systemic: Concurrent cisplatin 100 mg/m2 q3w (based on pooled EORTC 22931 / RTOG 9501 trials demonstrating local-regional and disease-free survival benefit)

peripheral_sbrt: 54 Gy in 3 fractions (18 Gy/fraction, BED10 = 151.2 Gy, EQD2 = 90 Gy)
48 Gy in 4 fractions (12 Gy/fraction, BED10 = 105.6 Gy, EQD2 = 56 Gy)
50 Gy in 5 fractions (10 Gy/fraction, BED10 = 100 Gy, EQD2 = 50 Gy)
central_sbrt_no_fly_zone: 50 to 60 Gy in 5 to 8 fractions (e.g. 50 Gy in 5 fx [10 Gy/fx] or 60 Gy in 8 fx [7.5 Gy/fx]) to avoid proximal bronchial tree and pulmonary artery necrosis (RTOG 0813)
56 Gy in 7 fractions (8 Gy/fraction) or 60 Gy in 15 fractions (4 Gy/fraction)

definitive_chemoradiation.dose: 60 to 66 Gy in 30 to 33 fractions (2.0 Gy/fraction) (RTOG 0617 confirmed 60 Gy is superior in overall survival compared to 74 Gy high-dose escalation due to cardiopulmonary toxicity)
definitive_chemoradiation.concurrent_chemotherapy: Platinum doublet (cisplatin 50 mg/m2 days 1, 8, 29, 36 + etoposide 50 mg/m2 days 1-5, 29-33 OR carboplatin AUC 2 + paclitaxel 45-50 mg/m2 weekly)
definitive_chemoradiation.consolidation_immunotherapy: Durvalumab 10 mg/kg q2w or 1500 mg q4w for up to 12 months in non-progressing patients (PACIFIC trial)

adjuvant_nsclc.port_indications: Generally reserved for unexpected microscopic positive surgical margins (R1: 54-60 Gy in 27-30 fx) or macroscopic residual (R2: 60-66 Gy). Routine PORT for resected pN2 R0 is NOT recommended based on Lung ART trial results unless clinical trial.

small_cell_lung_cancer.limited_stage_definitive: 45 Gy in 30 fractions BID (1.5 Gy twice daily over 3 weeks, gap >=6h) concurrent with cisplatin/etoposide (Turrisi NEJM trial), or 60-66 Gy in 30-33 daily fractions (2.0 Gy/fx)
small_cell_lung_cancer.prophylactic_cranial_irradiation: 25 Gy in 10 fractions (2.5 Gy/fx) for patients with good response to chemo-RT

adjuvant_whole_breast_irradiation.moderate_hypofractionation_standard: 40.05 Gy in 15 fractions (2.67 Gy/fraction) over 3 weeks or 42.56 Gy in 16 fractions (2.66 Gy/fx)
adjuvant_whole_breast_irradiation.ultra_hypofractionation_fast_forward: 26 Gy in 5 fractions over 1 week (5.2 Gy/fraction daily) (FAST-Forward trial 10-year data showing non-inferiority in local control and normal tissue cosmesis)
adjuvant_whole_breast_irradiation.conventional_fractionation: 45 to 50 Gy in 25 fractions (1.8-2.0 Gy/fx) over 5 weeks (historical standard, now reserved for complex anatomy or specific reconstructions)

tumor_bed_boost.dose: 10 to 16 Gy in 4 to 8 fractions (2.0 Gy/fx) sequential or simultaneous integrated boost (SIB)
tumor_bed_boost.indications: Age <= 50, high grade (Grade 3), close surgical margins (<2 mm), extensive intraductal component (EIC)

post_mastectomy_radiation_therapy.indications: >=4 positive axillary lymph nodes, T3-T4 primary tumor, or 1-3 positive nodes with adverse features (MA.20 / EORTC 22922 / EBCTCG meta-analysis)
post_mastectomy_radiation_therapy.target_volumes: Chest wall and regional lymph nodes (supraclavicular fossa, internal mammary chain, +/- axillary levels I-III if incompletely dissected)
post_mastectomy_radiation_therapy.dose: 50 Gy in 25 fractions (2.0 Gy/fx) or hypofractionated 40.05 Gy in 15 fractions (2.67 Gy/fx) +/- scar boost (10 Gy in 5 fx)

accelerated_partial_breast_irradiation.criteria: ASTRO low-risk consensus: age >= 50, unicentric, ER+, ductal histology, <=2 cm (T1), negative margins >= 2 mm, pN0
accelerated_partial_breast_irradiation.regimens: 30 Gy in 5 fractions every other day (6 Gy/fx) or 26 Gy in 5 fractions daily

low_risk: Moderate hypofractionation: 60 Gy in 20 fractions (3.0 Gy/fx) over 4 weeks (CHHiP, PROFIT) or 70 Gy in 28 fractions (2.5 Gy/fx)
Ultra-hypofractionated SBRT: 36.25 Gy in 5 fractions (7.25 Gy/fx) or 35 Gy in 5 fractions (7.0 Gy/fx) (PACE-B, HYPO-RT-PC)
Conventional dose escalation: 75.6 to 79.2 Gy in 39 to 44 fractions (1.8-2.0 Gy/fx)

intermediate_risk.favorable: 60 Gy in 20 fx or 36.25 Gy in 5 fx SBRT without ADT
intermediate_risk.unfavorable: 60 Gy in 20 fx or 78 Gy in 39 fx + 4 to 6 months short-term Androgen Deprivation Therapy (ADT) +/- pelvic nodal RT (45-50.4 Gy)

high_and_very_high_risk.radiotherapy: 78 to 80 Gy in 39-40 fractions (or 60 Gy in 20 fx) to prostate + 46-50 Gy to pelvic lymph nodes
high_and_very_high_risk.systemic_therapy: Long-term ADT (24 to 36 months) with LHRH agonist/antagonist +/- abiraterone acetate for very high risk (STAMPEDE trial)

post_prostatectomy.salvage_vs_adjuvant: Early salvage at PSA >0.1-0.2 ng/mL is equivalent in event-free survival to routine adjuvant RT while sparing unnecessary toxicity (RADICALS-RT, RAVES, GETUG-AFU 17 meta-analysis ARTISTIC)
post_prostatectomy.dose: 64.8 to 66 Gy in 32 to 36 fractions (1.8-2.0 Gy/fx) to prostatic fossa; 70-72 Gy for gross recurrent disease; 45-50.4 Gy to pelvic lymph nodes for high-risk features

esophagus.neoadjuvant_trimodality: 41.4 Gy in 23 fractions (1.8 Gy/fx) with concurrent weekly carboplatin (AUC 2) + paclitaxel (50 mg/m2) (CROSS trial standard)
esophagus.definitive_chemoradiation: 50.0 to 50.4 Gy in 25 to 28 fractions (1.8-2.0 Gy/fx) with concurrent cisplatin + 5-FU or FOLFOX (RTOG 85-01 / PRODIGE 5)

total_neoadjuvant_therapy.short_course_rt: 25 Gy in 5 fractions (5.0 Gy/fx) over 1 week, followed by consolidation chemotherapy (CAPOX/FOLFOX x 4-6 cycles) prior to TME or Watch-and-Wait (RAPIDO / STELLAR trials)
total_neoadjuvant_therapy.long_course_chemoradiation: 50.0 to 50.4 Gy in 25 to 28 fractions (1.8-2.0 Gy/fx) with concurrent capecitabine (825 mg/m2 BID) or 5-FU, followed by consolidation chemotherapy (PRODIGE 23 / OPRA trial)

definitive_chemoradiation_nigro.primary_and_gross_nodes: 50.4 to 54.0 Gy in 28 to 30 fractions (1.8 Gy/fx) for T1-T2; 54.0 to 59.4 Gy in 30 to 33 fractions for T3-T4 / N+
definitive_chemoradiation_nigro.concurrent_chemotherapy: Mitomycin-C (10-12 mg/m2 IV bolus days 1 and 29) + 5-FU (1000 mg/m2/day continuous infusion days 1-4 and 29-32) or capecitabine

pancreas.borderline_or_locally_advanced: 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions (1.8 Gy/fx) with capecitabine or gemcitabine, or hypofractionated SBRT 33 to 40 Gy in 5 fractions

cervix_locally_advanced.definitive_ebrt: 45.0 Gy in 25 fractions (1.8 Gy/fx) to whole pelvis +/- para-aortic nodes (45 Gy) with concurrent weekly cisplatin (40 mg/m2 IV x 5-6 cycles)
cervix_locally_advanced.brachytherapy_boost: Image-Guided Adaptive Brachytherapy (IGABT) HDR (e.g. 28 Gy in 4 fractions or 21 Gy in 3 fractions) delivering cumulative High-Risk CTV (HR-CTV) D90 >= 85 to 90 Gy EQD2 (alpha/beta = 10 Gy) (EMBRACE I & II protocols)
cervix_locally_advanced.normal_tissue_constraints_eqd2: Rectum D2cc <= 65-70 Gy EQD2, Bladder D2cc <= 80-85 Gy EQD2, Sigmoid D2cc <= 70-75 Gy EQD2 (alpha/beta = 3 Gy)

endometrium_postoperative.vaginal_cuff_brachytherapy: For high-intermediate risk (PORTEC-1/2): HDR 21 Gy in 3 fractions (7 Gy/fx at 0.5 cm depth) or 15 Gy in 3 fractions at cylinder surface
endometrium_postoperative.pelvic_ebrt: 45.0 to 50.4 Gy in 25 to 28 fractions (1.8 Gy/fx) for positive nodes, deep myometrial invasion with high grade/LVSI, cervical stromal invasion (PORTEC-3: Pelvic EBRT + concurrent/adjuvant cisplatin/carboplatin)

glioblastoma.standard_stupp_regimen: 60.0 Gy in 30 fractions (2.0 Gy/fx) with concurrent temozolomide (75 mg/m2 daily) followed by 6 cycles maintenance temozolomide (150-200 mg/m2 days 1-5 q28d) +/- Tumor Treating Fields (TTF)
glioblastoma.elderly_or_poor_performance: Hypofractionated RT 40.0 Gy in 15 fractions (2.67 Gy/fx) with concurrent and adjuvant temozolomide (Perry et al. NEJM trial) or 34 Gy in 10 fractions (Roa et al.)

low_grade_glioma.high_risk_lgg: 54.0 Gy in 30 fractions (1.8 Gy/fx) followed by adjuvant PCV chemotherapy (RTOG 9802 showing 5.5 year OS benefit)

stereotactic_radiosurgery_srs: Single fraction (RTOG 9005): <=20 mm: 24 Gy; 21-30 mm: 18 Gy; 31-40 mm: 15 Gy
Fractionated stereotactic RT (FSRT): 27-30 Gy in 3 fractions (9-10 Gy/fx) or 30 Gy in 5 fractions (6 Gy/fx) for large metastases (>2-3 cm) or postoperative resection cavity to reduce radionecrosis
brain_metastases.whole_brain_rt: 30.0 Gy in 10 fractions (3.0 Gy/fx) or 20 Gy in 5 fractions (4.0 Gy/fx) with hippocampal avoidance (HA-WBRT: NRG CC001) + memantine for preserved neurocognition

target_volume_specifications.gtv: Gross Tumor Volume: Gross demonstrable extent and location of malignant growth (clinical, endoscopic, or radiological).
target_volume_specifications.ctv: Clinical Target Volume: Tissue volume that contains a GTV and/or subclinical microscopic malignant disease (margins typically 5-10 mm anatomically constrained).
target_volume_specifications.itv: Internal Target Volume: CTV plus internal margin accounting for physiologic motion (respiration, bladder/rectal filling).
target_volume_specifications.ptv: Planning Target Volume: Geometric concept accounting for net effect of all setup uncertainties and organ variations (typically 3-5 mm around CTV/ITV depending on IGRT frequency).
target_volume_specifications.oar: Organ At Risk: Normal tissue whose radiation sensitivity significantly influences treatment planning and/or prescribed dose.
target_volume_specifications.prv: Planning Organ at Risk Volume: Margin added to OAR to account for setup and motion variations.

drug_radiation_interaction_mechanisms.spatial_cooperation: Chemotherapy treats distant micrometastases outside the radiation portal, while radiation treats primary local-regional disease.
drug_radiation_interaction_mechanisms.toxicity_independence: Different organ toxicity profiles allow full therapeutic doses of both modalities without synergistic normal tissue destruction.

radiosensitization.mechanism: Inhibits sublethal DNA damage repair, stabilizes radiation-induced DNA double-strand breaks, synchronizes cells into radiosensitive G2/M phase, active in hypoxic cells.
Thymidylate synthase inhibition depletes dTMP, producing severe DNA repair failure and radiosensitization during S phase.
Methylates guanine at O6 position; concurrent radiation produces single and double strand breaks that trigger futile mismatch repair and apoptotic death (enhanced in MGMT promoter methylated tumors).
Stabilizes microtubules, arresting proliferating tumor cells in the highly radiosensitive G2/M phase of the cell cycle.

canonical_target_prescriptions_summary.prescribed_dose: 70 Gy / 35 fx (high risk GTV), 59.5-63 Gy / 35 fx (intermediate risk), 54-56 Gy / 35 fx (elective low risk nodes)
canonical_target_prescriptions_summary.concurrent_agent: Cisplatin 100 mg/m2 q3w x 3 or weekly 40 mg/m2

40.05 Gy / 15 fx or 26 Gy / 5 fx (FAST-Forward) +/- boost 10-16 Gy
canonical_target_prescriptions_summary.concurrent_agent: Sequential endocrine therapy or chemotherapy (concurrent RT + chemo avoided)

canonical_target_prescriptions_summary.prescribed_dose: 50 Gy / 25 fx or 40.05 Gy / 15 fx to chest wall and supraclavicular/internal mammary nodes
60 Gy / 20 fx or 78 Gy / 39 fx +/- pelvic nodes 46-50 Gy
canonical_target_prescriptions_summary.concurrent_agent: Short-term (4-6 mo) or long-term (24-36 mo) ADT

canonical_target_prescriptions_summary.prescribed_dose: 64.8-66 Gy in 32-36 fx to prostatic fossa
canonical_target_prescriptions_summary.concurrent_agent: +/- short-term ADT (6 months) for high-risk features

canonical_target_prescriptions_summary.clinical_scenario: Locally advanced rectal cancer (cT3-4 or N+)
canonical_target_prescriptions_summary.prescribed_dose: Short course (25 Gy / 5 fx) or Long course (50.4 Gy / 28 fx) with TNT consolidation
canonical_target_prescriptions_summary.concurrent_agent: Capecitabine (with long course) or systemic consolidation (CAPOX/FOLFOX)

canonical_target_prescriptions_summary.clinical_scenario: Definitive anal canal squamous cell carcinoma

canonical_target_prescriptions_summary.prescribed_dose: 45 Gy / 25 fx pelvic EBRT + IGABT HDR boost to HR-CTV total EQD2 >= 85-90 Gy
60 Gy / 30 fx (Stupp) or 40 Gy / 15 fx (elderly/poor PS)
SRS 18-24 Gy single fraction or FSRT 27-30 Gy / 3 fx or 30 Gy / 5 fx
